newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD wants Kohl to face confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: German SPD wants Kohl to face confidence vote.

text.p: A leading member of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) has called on Chancellor Helmut Kohl to link a parliamentary vote in July on his 1998 budget with a confidence motion, a newspaper said on Thursday.
If Kohl were to lose such a confidence vote the way could be opened for general elections scheduled for next September to be brought forward a year.

"If the Chancellor can no longer manage his business properly then he should have the courage to go before the Bundestag (lower house) and ask the confidence question," Peter Struck, SPD parliamentary whip told the Bildwoche weekly.

Kohl's coalition of Christian Democrats (CDU), Christian Social Union (CSU) and Free Democrats (FDP) are currently trying to hammer out a deal on the 1998 budget which will raise funds to fill widening budget deficits.

They must agree by July 10 so that a budget bill can be put to parliament the following day, but negotiations have strained the coalition because the liberal FDP are firmly opposed to any increases in taxes to help balance the books.

Struck said the FDP had to put itself on the line. Either the party would betray its tax-cutting principles and follow the CDU/CSU into election defeat or vote against the Chancellor and show its commitment to lower taxes, he said.
Struck said if the Chancellor lost a confidence vote the SDP could be ready for an election by the end of September.

But CSU parliamentary whip Eduard Oswald said Struck's suggestion was a cheap attempt to distract attention from divisions and discord within the SPD and said Kohl had the confidence of all three coalition partners.

"The SPD doesn't even have a chancellor candidate, not to speak of a viable programme. The coalition and federal government on the other hand are acting in the interest of the future abilities of Germany," Oswald said in a statement.
"The coalition will present a budget which conforms with the constitution in July, which will be met with the agreement of the whole coalition," he said.
